The one thing that breaks it is a soaked Saturday track, because water flattens a car advantage and hands the day to whoever gambles best. He also owes this circuit something: the last time he raced here he put a Ferrari in the barrier and collected ten seconds and two penalty points for it.

Ferrari, based on track record alone, are most probably not winning this championship. However Hamilton is only fifty points down with twelve rounds to go, which with a little luck, a seven-time world champion's cut-throat discipline and a few more Mercedes DNFs doesn't seem that out of reach. The instruction is simple enough: put a car on the front row on Saturday, then finish the race. However, Ferrari's launches off the line this year may show us something Zandvoort has not produced since it came back: a winner who did not start from pole. The last time that happened was Lauda, from tenth, in 1985. Unfortunately, last year Hamilton binned it at Turn 3 on his own, which for a seven-time world champion at the circuit where he holds the race lap record is indefensible. Leclerc also DNF'd, at least with the excuse of being hit by Mercedes' prodigy, which gave us yet another [immortal meme](https://autos.yahoo.com/articles/charles-leclerc-mercilessly-mocked-crashing-193000705.html) of the Monegasque's depressed demeanour.

Verstappen needs one lap to go right. [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) are fourth with 177 points and he has 109 of them. Three wins here, three poles, no other route in. A soaked track is his best friend on Saturday and the crowd is worth something on Sunday, but if he is not on the front row, the send-off is a fight for the podium and a lap of honour.

## Where it leaves us

**For the books:** the 36th and final championship Dutch Grand Prix, Zandvoort's first and only sprint, Verstappen's last home race, Antonelli's last as a teenager, and Lawson's first Red Bull start since 2025.

Twelve grands prix run from here to the season finale. We might be waving goodbye to Zandvoort but it's not going down without a fight, offering drivers who perform masterclasses in the wet, such as the home hero in [Max Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen) and [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari)'s [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton), a chance to give us a memory that can't be forgotten.

Session times, live and in your own timezone, are on the [weekend page](/series/f1/weekend/12), the race starts at 15:00 local, and it is on [F1 TV](https://f1tv.formula1.com/). Zandvoort came back onto the calendar because of one driver, and it leaves with him still looking for his first win of the year. The question is whether he takes it here, or whether Zandvoort says goodbye to him the way it has to everyone else who did not start from pole. You never can know with Zandvoort.

Croes / Anefo, [CC BY-SA 3.0 NL](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Podium_at_1975_Dutch_Grand_Prix.jpg) (1975 podium), both via Wikimedia Commons.*

title: Russell wins Sprint: A boring Saturday morning, as the sprint format doesn't suit all tracks
summary: George Russell led every lap that mattered of the first and last sprint race Zandvoort will ever hold. Charles Leclerc took second off Lando Norris with a real overtake at Turn 1, Nico Hulkenberg's Audi broke, and the shower everybody had watched all morning arrived as the winner crossed the line.
body:
[George Russell](/drivers/george-russell) started the first sprint race Zandvoort has ever held from pole and won the only one it will ever hold from the front. Twenty-four laps, [30:25.318](https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2026/races/1292/netherlands/sprint-results), 1.360s in hand, and a shower that had been hanging over the dunes all morning arriving at the exact moment he crossed the line. If you were scripting a farewell you would probably not dare.

He got the launch right, led into Turn 1, and had 1.6s by lap 10. The lead moved around a little after that without ever looking like it was in danger. It is the third time he has turned a sprint pole into a sprint win, and given he took that pole having [topped neither q1 or q2](https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/dutch-gp-f1-sprint-qualifying-2026-russell-pole/) on Friday, the whole weekend so far has been Russell finding speed exactly when the timing screens are live.

|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | George Russell | Mercedes | 30:25.318 | 8 |
| 2 | Charles Leclerc | Ferrari | +1.360 | 7 |
| 3 | Lando Norris | McLaren | +5.196 | 6 |
| 4 | Kimi Antonelli | Mercedes | +5.581 | 5 |
| 5 | Oscar Piastri | McLaren | +10.185 | 4 |
| 6 | Max Verstappen | Red Bull | +10.529 | 3 |
| 7 | Lewis Hamilton | Ferrari | +12.188 | 2 |
| 8 | Pierre Gasly | Alpine | +42.510 | 1 |
| 9 | Gabriel Bortoleto | Audi | +44.437 | |
| 10 | Arvid Lindblad | Racing Bulls | +44.971 | |
| 11 | Liam Lawson | Red Bull | +47.471 | |
| 12 | Franco Colapinto | Alpine | +54.466 | |
| 13 | Yuki Tsunoda | Racing Bulls | +56.483 | |
| 14 | Esteban Ocon | Haas | +66.098 | |
| 15 | Oliver Bearman | Haas | +66.588 | |
| 16 | Alexander Albon | Williams | +74.632 | |

| 20 | Carlos Sainz | Williams | +1 lap | |
| 21 | Sergio Perez | Cadillac | +3 laps | |
| DNF | Nico Hulkenberg | Audi | 7 laps, power unit | |

## Leclerc went and took it

The race behind him was better. [Lando Norris](/drivers/lando-norris) held second for seventeen laps with [Charles Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) sitting inside a couple of tenths of the McLaren for most of them, close enough to be a nuisance and never quite close enough to do anything. On lap 18 he stopped waiting, put the [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) down the inside at Turn 1 and made it stick. Friday's sprint qualifying had [put those two within 0.055s of each other](https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/f1-dutch-gp-sprint-qualifying-report/10847946/), so the pass had been coming since the timing screens went live the day before.

At a circuit whose entire reputation is that overtaking does not happen there, that is worth more than one position. Leclerc had also started on softs, one of only two drivers who did, everybody else having gone for mediums. Ferrari looked at one hour of practice, made a call nobody else made, and finished second with it. On a weekend where their qualifying pace kept letting them down, their race thinking did not.

Norris held third at +5.196 and [Kimi Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) could not find a way past him, coming home fourth at +5.581 after taking [Oscar Piastri](/drivers/oscar-piastri) at Turn 2 on the opening lap. Piastri was fifth, [Max Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen) sixth at +10.529 with [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton) briefly all over the back of him, and Hamilton seventh.

## The last point, and then a cliff

[Pierre Gasly](/drivers/pierre-gasly) took the eighth and final point for [Alpine](/teams/alpine) at +42.510, which tells you how quickly this field spread out once the top seven had settled. [Gabriel Bortoleto](/drivers/gabriel-bortoleto) was ninth at +44.437 and under investigation for an unsafe release, [Arvid Lindblad](/drivers/arvid-lindblad) tenth, and [Liam Lawson](/drivers/liam-lawson) eleventh in the Red Bull.

Three cars had their weekend decided before the lights. [Carlos Sainz](/drivers/carlos-sainz) and [Fernando Alonso](/drivers/fernando-alonso) both started from the pit lane, and not for the ordinary reason: both [Williams](/teams/williams) and [Aston Martin](/teams/aston-martin) changed setup under parc fermé without the Technical Delegate's approval, which carries a mandatory sanction. [Williams did it](https://www.gpblog.com/en/breaking-news/pit-lane-start-for-sainz-as-williams-breaks-parc-ferme-to-reset-difficult-dutch-gp-weekend) because Sainz's three trips into the gravel on Friday had damaged his floor badly enough that the team wanted the suspension rethought overnight; [Aston Martin did the same thing](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/sainz-alonso-start-pit-lane-094020064.html) with a car that had already qualified last. [Sergio Pérez](/drivers/sergio-perez)'s [Cadillac](/teams/cadillac) needed repairs in the pit lane before the formation lap had finished and he came home three laps down.

[Nico Hulkenberg](/drivers/nico-hulkenberg) lasted seven laps, after a power unit failure ended the [Audi](/teams/audi) that had been the quiet story of Friday practice, seventh fastest on the medium compound while everyone ahead used softs. The one session where Audi looked genuinely well prepared was followed by the one result that made it irrelevant.

## What it did to the fight behind Antonelli

Nothing changed at the top and everything tightened underneath it. Antonelli still leads, and he spent the sprint in fourth watching two of the three men chasing him score more than he did.

Russell took the maximum eight and moved to 168. Hamilton took two and sits on 171. **Three points** now separate them in the fight for second in the championship, and they are not team-mates, which is the part that will make the rest of the season interesting. Leclerc's seven took him to 145 and Norris' six to 134, so the four drivers behind Antonelli are covered by 37 points with twelve rounds left. Antonelli's own lead is 53 over Hamilton and 56 over Russell: still comfortable, no longer serene.

Worth saying plainly, because the arithmetic is the story: [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) have the championship leader and the man closing fastest on second place, and they are in the same garage. Zandvoort's sprint was the first weekend this season where that has looked like a question rather than a luxury. The [teams' own verdicts](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/what-the-teams-said-sprint-day-and-qualifying-in-the-netherlands-2026.1vJ9dLmIstL3qivbyY0OEu) on the day are worth reading side by side.

Russell's own read afterwards was not triumphant. "Obviously a great start to the weekend. The Ferraris look fast so it's gonna be tight this afternoon," he told [Formula 1](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/russell-surges-to-victory-in-zandvoort-sprint-ahead-of-leclerc-and-norris.3evWfVZ0yONnfGGp3t8qyK). He was right that it would be tight and wrong about who from. Ferrari were nowhere near pole a few hours later. Norris was.

## Where it leaves us

**For the books:** the first and last sprint race in Zandvoort's history, Russell's third sprint win, his third sprint pole converted, Leclerc's soft-tyre gamble paying off with the only real overtake of the afternoon, and rain arriving on the chequered flag rather than a lap before it.

The full order is on the [sprint page](/series/f1/weekend/12/sprint), the running totals on the [standings](/series/f1/standings), and the rest of the weekend on the [Dutch Grand Prix hub](/series/f1/weekend/12). The [grid it produced](https://www.crash.net/f1/news/1102700/1/f1-2026-dutch-grand-prix-full-starting-grid-zandvoort-sprint-race) is on Crash.

Zandvoort held one sprint race in its life, gave it a four-hundredths pole, an overtake at a corner where overtakes are not supposed to happen, and rain timed to the second. For a circuit accused of being boring, it is going out with a certain amount of nerve.

*Photo: Steffen Prößdorf, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:2024-08-24_Motorsport,_Formel_1,_Gro%C3%9Fer_Preis_der_Niederlande_2024_STP_3369_by_Stepro.jpg), via Wikimedia Commons.*

title: One hour practice is rarely enough: Antonelli leads the only practice, Russell steals sprint pole
summary: Zandvoort's farewell gave the field sixty minutes of running before it started counting for real. Kimi Antonelli used them best, Max Verstappen spent them eleventh, and George Russell went quickest in the one session where he had looked slowest all day.
body:
Formula 1 came back from four weeks off and gave itself sixty minutes to work out a circuit it will never come back to. That is the arithmetic of a sprint weekend, and [Zandvoort](/series/f1/weekend/12) got the fifth of this season's six for the last event it will ever hold. One hour of practice, then parc fermé shuts, then everything counts. Whatever the setup sheets said at the end of that hour is roughly what twenty-two cars raced all weekend.

[Kimi Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) read it quickest. A 1:12.949 was the only lap all session under 1m13s, and it landed in the closing minutes on his second flying run on softs after traffic ruined the first. He had already spun at the exit of Turn 10 by then, which he explained over the radio with admirable economy: "I don't know what happened there." The championship leader, half a second of drama and then the fastest lap of the day. It is becoming a habit.

## The order nobody had time to argue with

[Lando Norris](/drivers/lando-norris) ended up second at +0.121, [George Russell](/drivers/george-russell) third at +0.125. Four thousandths of a second between a McLaren and the second Mercedes, which on a Friday means nothing and by Saturday evening meant everything. [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton) was fourth and [Charles Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) fifth, so [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) had both cars in the top five before the weekend had properly started, and [Oscar Piastri](/drivers/oscar-piastri) was sixth at +0.659, the first driver more than half a second adrift.

| Pos | Driver | Team | Gap | Laps |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | Kimi Antonelli | Mercedes | 1:12.949 | 36 |
| 2 | Lando Norris | McLaren | +0.121 | 30 |
| 3 | George Russell | Mercedes | +0.125 | 37 |
| 4 | Lewis Hamilton | Ferrari | +0.190 | 34 |
| 5 | Charles Leclerc | Ferrari | +0.289 | 39 |
| 6 | Oscar Piastri | McLaren | +0.659 | 35 |
| 7 | Nico Hulkenberg | Audi | +0.835 | 34 |
| 8 | Pierre Gasly | Alpine | +0.962 | 28 |
| 9 | Gabriel Bortoleto | Audi | +1.043 | 29 |
| 10 | Arvid Lindblad | Racing Bulls | +1.336 | 37 |
| 11 | Max Verstappen | Red Bull | +1.376 | 25 |

Below that: Alonso twelfth, Colapinto thirteenth, Lawson fourteenth on his first run in the car, Bearman fifteenth, Ocon sixteenth, Tsunoda seventeenth, Stroll eighteenth, Albon nineteenth, Bottas twentieth, Perez twenty-first and Sainz twenty-second.

The session had opened wet. The track was declared as such, damp patches were scattered around the lap, and the early runners went out on intermediates before it dried underneath them fast enough that Piastri was on mediums five minutes in. Rain was threatening again by the end. [The Race called it](https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/what-happened-in-only-dutch-gp-f1-2026-practice-session/) exactly what it was: not enough running, in the wrong conditions, before the part that mattered.

Nobody had a worse hour than [Carlos Sainz](/drivers/carlos-sainz). Into the gravel at Turn 13, then wide again at Turn 11, floor damage on the [Williams](/teams/williams), and last of everybody at +3.396. It cost him more than a Friday: the repairs pushed Williams into overnight suspension changes, the changes broke parc fermé, and [Sainz started the sprint from the pit lane](https://www.gpblog.com/en/breaking-news/pit-lane-start-for-sainz-as-williams-breaks-parc-ferme-to-reset-difficult-dutch-gp-weekend) as a result. One excursion, one weekend gone.

## Audi did the clever thing

Look at seventh and ninth on that sheet. [Nico Hulkenberg](/drivers/nico-hulkenberg) at +0.835 and [Gabriel Bortoleto](/drivers/gabriel-bortoleto) at +1.043, and both of them set those times on the **medium** compound while the cars around them were on softs. On a weekend with one practice session, that is a team that arrived knowing what it wanted and spent the hour confirming it rather than searching. [Audi](/teams/audi) have not had many afternoons like that this year.

It did not last, which is the cruel part. Hulkenberg's sprint ended after seven laps with a power unit failure, and the car that had looked the most composed thing on the circuit on Friday lunchtime never got to show it.

## Eleventh, at his own farewell

[Max Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen) has won this race three times since it returned in 2021 and finished second in the other two. It is the best record anyone has at the modern Zandvoort by a distance, this is the last Dutch Grand Prix the circuit will host, and he ended the only practice session of the weekend eleventh, 1.376s off the pace, after running wide at Turn 13.

Red Bull arrived rearranged too. [Liam Lawson](/drivers/liam-lawson) was in the second car because [Isack Hadjar](/drivers/isack-hadjar) is out, the Frenchman having [reportedly fractured his wrist](https://www.planetf1.com/news/isack-hadjar-wrist-injury-fresh-details-dutch-gp) on a heavy bag in the gym over the break, which is a sentence that should not appear in a Formula 1 season report and yet here we are. It costs [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) a driver sitting eighth in the [championship](/series/f1/standings) on 68 points. Lawson had never driven the 2026 car and was handed it on a weekend containing one hour of practice; he was fourteenth. Yuki Tsunoda, who started the year without a seat anywhere, came back at [Racing Bulls](/teams/racing-bulls) and was seventeenth.

## Then Russell produced a lap out of nowhere

Sprint qualifying is where Friday stopped being preparation. Russell had topped neither segment: Leclerc headed the first, Piastri the second, and Russell was somewhere behind both. With four minutes left Norris went out into clean air and took provisional pole, and then Russell answered with a **1:11.567** and beat it by **0.041s**.

| Pos | Driver | Team | SQ3 |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | George Russell | Mercedes | 1:11.567 |
| 2 | Lando Norris | McLaren | 1:11.608 |
| 3 | Charles Leclerc | Ferrari | 1:11.622 |
| 4 | Oscar Piastri | McLaren | 1:11.666 |
| 5 | Kimi Antonelli | Mercedes | 1:11.794 |
| 6 | Max Verstappen | Red Bull | 1:12.094 |
| 7 | Lewis Hamilton | Ferrari | 1:12.191 |
| 8 | Pierre Gasly | Alpine | 1:12.578 |
| 9 | Gabriel Bortoleto | Audi | 1:12.583 |
| 10 | Arvid Lindblad | Racing Bulls | 1:12.737 |

Knocked out in SQ2: Lawson, Tsunoda, Colapinto, Hulkenberg, Ocon, Albon. Out in SQ1: Bearman, Sainz, Stroll, Bottas, Perez and Alonso.

Behind those two, Leclerc was third at +0.055 and Piastri fourth at +0.099. The whole front two rows of the sprint grid inside a tenth of a second. [Motorsport.com described it](https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/f1-dutch-gp-sprint-qualifying-report/10847946/) as a tight sprint pole and that undersells it: at a circuit with this reputation for processional racing, Zandvoort's only sprint grid was set by four hundredths.

It was Russell's third sprint pole of the season from five sprint weekends, after China and Canada, and he would go on to convert this one the way he converted China. [Sky's framing](https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/13575268/dutch-gp-sprint-qualifying-george-russell-claims-pole-position-with-title-rivals-kimi-antonelli-lewis-hamilton-on-back-foot) was the useful one: his title rivals were on the back foot, and one of them was his team-mate.

![Max Verstappen on track at Circuit Zandvoort](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Max_Verstappen_-_Circuit_Zandvoort_-_Jumbo_Race_Dagen_2018_Driven_by_Max_Verstappen_%2828406624178%29.jpg/1280px-Max_Verstappen_-_Circuit_Zandvoort_-_Jumbo_Race_Dagen_2018_Driven_by_Max_Verstappen_%2828406624178%29.jpg)

*Zandvoort in orange, the way the circuit earned its way back onto the calendar. Friday afternoon put the man it was rebuilt for sixth on the sprint grid.*

## Antonelli broke his own Friday

The championship leader's afternoon fell apart before most people noticed. He slid off into the gravel at the penultimate corner during the first phase of sprint qualifying, carried floor damage out of it, and could only manage fifth on his final run at +0.227. Fifth is not a disaster. Fifth with a damaged floor, at the circuit where he collected two penalty points last year for putting Leclerc into a barrier, on a weekend where second place in the championship is genuinely in play behind him, is a Friday he will want back.

Verstappen was sixth, more than half a second off Russell. [Aston Martin](/teams/aston-martin) had the worst of it: new Honda hardware, a scrappy hour, [Fernando Alonso](/drivers/fernando-alonso) locking up at Turn 1 and running wide, and twenty-second on the sheet. He too would start the sprint from the pit lane, for [the same parc fermé breach as Williams](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/sainz-alonso-start-pit-lane-094020064.html).

## What Friday actually told us

Two things, and they pointed in different directions. [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) had the fastest car and the fastest single lap, and they belonged to different drivers, which is a good problem until it is a points problem. And the field was so tightly packed after one hour of running that the sprint grid came down to hundredths, which is not what anyone expects from a circuit whose great criticism is that nothing happens on it.

**For the books:** Zandvoort's first and only sprint qualifying session, the last Friday of Formula 1 the circuit will ever stage, Lawson's first Friday in a 2026 Red Bull, and a 1:12.949 that stood as the only sub-1m13s lap of the day.

Session by session detail sits on the [Friday practice](/series/f1/weekend/12/practice-1) and [sprint qualifying](/series/f1/weekend/12/sprint-qualifying) pages, with the running order for the rest of the weekend on the [Dutch Grand Prix hub](/series/f1/weekend/12) and the season's totals on the [standings](/series/f1/standings).

One hour to learn a circuit, and the two men who used it best did not end up on the same row. Zandvoort was never going to go quietly.

*Photos: Yu Chu Chin, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mercedes-AMG_F1_W17_E_Performance_of_Andrea_Kimi_Antonelli_(028A8057).jpg) (hero); Danny Tax Creative, [CC BY 2.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Max_Verstappen_-_Circuit_Zandvoort_-_Jumbo_Race_Dagen_2018_Driven_by_Max_Verstappen_%2828406624178%29.jpg) (Zandvoort), both via Wikimedia Commons.*

title: Norris clinches pole position: as neither Mercedes improve under worsening conditions
summary: George Russell had already beaten Lando Norris twice at Zandvoort, by four hundredths for sprint pole and by 1.3 seconds in the sprint itself. With rain falling through the closing minutes of qualifying, Norris found a 1:11.163 and put a McLaren on the front for the circuit's final Grand Prix.
body:
By the time qualifying began, [George Russell](/drivers/george-russell) had beaten [Lando Norris](/drivers/lando-norris) twice in two days at a circuit neither of them will visit again. Four hundredths for sprint pole on Friday afternoon. Then 1.360s in the sprint itself on Saturday morning, from the front, in control. Norris got the last word, and he got it in the one set of conditions where getting it is hardest.

Rain was falling through the closing minutes. Grip was leaving the track rather than arriving on it, which is the version of a late qualifying run where the fast lap is the one you have already done, not the one you are about to attempt. Norris went out anyway and produced a [**1:11.163**](https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2026/races/1292/netherlands/qualifying), and Russell's answer was 0.102s short. "I was pushing because every one-hundredth can make a big difference in the end," Norris [told Formula 1](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/norris-denies-russell-pole-position-in-gripping-conclusion-to-qualifying-for-dutch-grand-prix.2DoHZDC14R5tY7ygGaHCz) afterwards, which on this occasion was a statement of method rather than a platitude. It is his second pole of the season.

## A tenth, covering four cars, for the second time in two days

| Pos | Driver | Team | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lando Norris | McLaren | 1:12.695 | 1:11.628 | 1:11.163 |

| 21 | Valtteri Bottas | Cadillac | 1:14.371 | | |
| 22 | Sergio Perez | Cadillac | 1:14.600 | | |

[Kimi Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) was third at +0.133, crucially behind teammate and championship contender George Russell, while [Oscar Piastri](/drivers/oscar-piastri) took his McLaren to fourth at +0.142. So the top four were inside 0.142s, having been [inside 0.099s in sprint qualifying](https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/dutch-gp-f1-sprint-qualifying-2026-russell-pole/) the day before. Two sessions, two days, four cars each time separated by roughly a tenth of a second, at the circuit everyone complains produces nothing.

Piastri's hour is the one worth staring at. He was the fastest man in the first phase on a 1:12.610 and second fastest in the second on a 1:11.641, and he qualified fourth. That is a driver who had the pace for fifty-eight minutes of an hour and did not have it for the two that counted, on a weekend where he has also been out-qualified and out-raced by his team-mate. [McLaren](/teams/mclaren) get the pole; the reigning champion is not the one having the smoother weekend of the two.

Antonelli, for his part, recovered a Friday he will want to forget. He put a wheel in the gravel in the first phase of sprint qualifying, carried floor damage through to fifth, then came back on Saturday and out-qualified both Ferraris. Third on the grid, 0.133s off pole, at the circuit where he collected two penalty points last year for putting Leclerc into a barrier. He is repaying that debt in instalments.

## Ferrari's weekend, in two contradictory numbers

[Charles Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) finished the sprint second, having taken the place off Norris with a real overtake at Turn 1 on lap 18. A few hours later he qualified sixth, four tenths off pole, behind [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton) in fifth.

That is the puzzle of [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) at Zandvoort and arguably of Ferrari in 2026. Quick when the race is long and the tyres matter, ordinary when it comes down to one lap on low fuel. If their sprint pace was the real thing, Leclerc starts Sunday from further back than the car deserves, at a circuit where every winner since it returned in 2021 has started from pole. That is not a small problem. It is the whole problem.

## Seventh, and within a tenth of the stand-in

[Max Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen) qualified seventh, 0.455s off pole, at the last Dutch Grand Prix Zandvoort will ever hold. Three wins here, all three from pole, and never a win from anywhere else. The fourth row is not where that record gets extended.

The number that will sting more sits directly behind him. [Liam Lawson](/drivers/liam-lawson) was eighth on a 1:11.733, which is **0.115s** off Verstappen, in a car he had never driven before Friday, on a weekend containing one hour of practice, having been called up at short notice because [Isack Hadjar](/drivers/isack-hadjar) is injured, the Frenchman having [reportedly fractured his wrist](https://www.planetf1.com/news/isack-hadjar-wrist-injury-fresh-details-dutch-gp) in the gym over the break. Read that as praise for Lawson or as a question about [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing)'s season; either reading is available and neither is comfortable.

At the back, [Aston Martin](/teams/aston-martin) put both cars out in the first phase with their upgraded Honda hardware, [Fernando Alonso](/drivers/fernando-alonso) eighteenth and [Lance Stroll](/drivers/lance-stroll) nineteenth, and both [Cadillacs](/teams/cadillac) filled the last row. [Carlos Sainz](/drivers/carlos-sainz) went out in the first phase too, seventeenth, closing a weekend that began with three trips into the gravel and a [pit-lane start in the sprint](https://www.gpblog.com/en/breaking-news/pit-lane-start-for-sainz-as-williams-breaks-parc-ferme-to-reset-difficult-dutch-gp-weekend) after Williams broke parc fermé to fix the damage.

## The grid, stays unchanged this time

No penalties reordered anybody. [The starting grid](https://racingnews365.com/full-starting-grid-for-2026-f1-dutch-grand-prix-at-zandvoort) reads exactly as qualifying finished, from Norris on pole to [Sergio Pérez](/drivers/sergio-perez) twenty-second, with one change: Pérez starts from the pit lane after a rule breach. He was last anyway, so it costs him little beyond the indignity.

Which means the front two rows are McLaren, Mercedes, Mercedes, McLaren, in that order. Mercedes had won eight of the eleven races before this weekend and took the first ten poles of the season; the front row here belongs to the team that ended that run in Hungary. [GPFans has the grid](https://www.gpfans.com/en/f1-news/1089376/f1-dutch-grand-prix-starting-grid-2026-all-penalties-applied/) with every penalty applied, for anyone who wants to check it against the timing sheet.

## Race day

Paddock's own hour-by-hour forecast had the 15:00 start at 19C with a 20% chance of rain, easing to 16% at 16:00 and 14% by 17:00, and it held. Dry, and drying further, the exact reverse of Saturday: rain on the sprint's chequered flag, a wet threat over qualifying, and then a clean Sunday.

That mattered more here than at most places. Water flattens a car advantage and hands a race to whoever gambles best. A dry track at Zandvoort hands it to whoever starts at the front, and since 2021 the man who started at the front has won every time. Norris made it six, though not on a straight line: Kimi Antonelli led most of the afternoon before Norris took it back. [The race recap has all of it](/blog/f1-dutch-grand-prix-2026-race-recap).

**For the books:** the last qualifying session in Zandvoort's Formula 1 history, Norris' second pole of 2026, a fourth consecutive session this weekend decided inside two tenths, and a stand-in Red Bull driver within 0.115s of a four-time world champion at that driver's home race.

The full order is on the [qualifying page](/series/f1/weekend/12/qualifying), Saturday morning's race is on the [sprint page](/series/f1/weekend/12/sprint), the [teams' reactions to both sessions](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/what-the-teams-said-sprint-day-and-qualifying-in-the-netherlands-2026.1vJ9dLmIstL3qivbyY0OEu) are worth a read, and the [Dutch Grand Prix hub](/series/f1/weekend/12) carries session times in your own timezone. Season totals sit on the [standings](/series/f1/standings).

Pole has won every Dutch Grand Prix since the circuit came back. On the last afternoon it will ever get, pole belongs to a McLaren, the crowd came for a Red Bull on the fourth row, and the forecast has taken away the one thing that could have scrambled it.

title: Norris takes the last Dutch Grand Prix, and Zandvoort loses Verstappen on lap one
summary: Lando Norris won the final Formula 1 race Circuit Zandvoort will hold, seventy-two laps after Max Verstappen put his Red Bull into the barrier at the last corner and stopped the race. Kimi Antonelli led most of it and finished second, with Mercedes moving George Russell aside to make sure of it.
body:
[Lando Norris](/drivers/lando-norris) did what champions do, and won the final Formula 1 race Circuit Zandvoort will hold: [2:04:44.859](https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2026/races/1292/netherlands/race-result) for seventy-two laps, 11.536s clear of [Kimi Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli), from pole set at 1:11.163. It is his second win in a row after [Hungary](/series/f1/results), and it took him most of the afternoon, because for the middle two thirds of the race he was not the one leading.

However, in great contrast to our predictions in [this weekend's preview blog](https://paddock-tracker.com/blog/f1-dutch-grand-prix-2026-preview) on a surface still damp from the morning and worsening due to a slight drizzle, [Max Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen) caught the white line on the inside of the banked final corner, lost the rear of the [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) and hit the outside barrier hard enough to [stop the race](https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/f1-dutch-gp-red-flagged-after-monster-max-verstappen-crash/). The car came back across the track in pieces, as wrecked as a car can be.

Zandvoort returned to the calendar in 2021 largely because of him, and it leaves the calendar having watched him crash out of its last race on lap one, in front of a grandstand full of orange. [Bortoleto](/drivers/gabriel-bortoleto) followed the same line as the 4-time champion, with a fate much less punishing, spinning 360° and managing to avoid all walls and cars. Whoever was still watching after 3 minutes of nonstop replays, was lucky enough to witness [Hulkenberg's cat-like response time](https://www.formula1.com/en/video/2026-dutch-grand-prix-near-miss-for-audi-as-hulkenberg-avoids-a-spinning-bortoleto.1874321285519268338) in avoiding Bortoleto's spinning monocoque.

Verstappen was luckily uninjured after the [dramatic crash](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/verstappen-reacts-to-dramatic-dutch-gp-crash-as-he-sums-up-disappointing-home-weekend.6nrEOE03YhjdJy6shRzAf1), was cleared at the medical centre, and apologised to his team on the radio and to the fans and media before leaving the track. Nobody at [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) offered a mechanical explanation afterwards and neither did he, as it was clearly driver error this time. His classification reads zero laps, his year growing worse with every result.

| Pos | Driver | Team | Gap | Pts |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | [Lando Norris](/drivers/lando-norris) | [McLaren](/teams/mclaren) | 2:04:44.859 | 25 |

## The restart changed the race twice

The red flag handed everybody a free strategy meeting. Norris used it to fit softs; [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) kept mediums on both cars. Then [Oliver Bearman](/drivers/oliver-bearman)'s power unit failed on the way round to the grid, the field had to complete another lap while his [Haas](/teams/haas) was cleared, and the race finally got going again from a standing start with two cars already gone.

Antonelli won the restart outright. He had already taken second off [George Russell](/drivers/george-russell) at the original start, and this time he went past Norris and kept going. Two starts, two places gained, no drama in either, which is a cold way to lead a championship and an effective one.

He led the first stop cycle and he led the second. What he could not do was hold the tyre advantage once [McLaren](/teams/mclaren) had one. Norris came back through in the final third, taking Antonelli into Turn 1 on the brakes and inheriting the lead moments later from [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton), who was ahead of them both on an offset strategy. From there it was a straight run to the flag.

## The order from the pit wall

Mercedes were never going to catch Norris. What they needed was a risky strategy, hoping to change their unavoidable fate. The call decided was to bring the Italian, Antonelli in for a risky late switch to softs, hoping to reach Norris' worn hards. A late virtual safety car for [Esteban Ocon](/drivers/esteban-ocon)'s stopped Haas gave them the cheap stop they needed, and they took it, fit the softs dropping him behind Russell, who stayed out on old hards. Russell had the audacity to ask for team orders, in other words no attack from Antonelli so he could calmly attack and maybe catch Norris. He then proceeded to finish nearly 16 seconds behind the reigning champion. Antonelli however soared past Russell quickly, as the pit wall told Russell to let him through. Interesting, watching a championship contender throw valuable points away just to fulfill his prophecy as Toto Wolff's pet. Some drivers are built to never win a championship, be forever remembered as the not so tough competition that great drivers fought amongst.

Russell at least did not do it immediately. He argued on the radio that swapping risked the double podium, then predictably complied, forcing him to have to defend third from (2nd in the championship) Hamilton and [Charles Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) all the way to the line on tyres that were finished. He finished 0.849s ahead of Hamilton after all that.

Afterwards he took the team's side. "Kimi was ahead of me anyway so he deserved to finish ahead," he [told Formula 1](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/you-want-to-fight-for-every-single-position-russell-offers-verdict-on-mercedes-team-orders-in-dutch-gp.3qBtPSF2Jgfyu63IKV8our), pointing out that Antonelli on new rubber would have taken the place regardless. Toto Wolff called second and third [damage limitation](https://www.crash.net/f1/news/1102960/1/tough-calls-need-be-done-toto-wolff-stands-mercedes-f1-team-orders) and Russell's closing defence "really, really exceptional", which it was. 

Our view: the swap was outrageous if he wants to consider himself a championship contender, his attempt at an argument was however fair. Three points between team-mates looks small in August. If Antonelli takes this title by fewer than three, nobody at Brackley will have to explain anything, and that is precisely why they did it. Russell will be the only person who will live with his mistake.

## A race that ate its own field

Only seven cars finished on the lead lap. Six retired, and the last of them was the most avoidable: in the closing laps [Carlos Sainz](/drivers/carlos-sainz) was defending from his own team-mate [Alexander Albon](/drivers/alexander-albon), who came around the outside at Turn 1. Sainz hit the bump on the inside harder than he expected, locked up, ran on and clipped him. Albon's floor was damaged and his race was over; Sainz took a ten-second penalty and, to his credit, no argument with it, calling it ["a fair penalty"](https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/carlos-sainz-explains-fair-penalty-for-alex-albon-contact-the-worst-possible-outcome/10848715/) and the outcome "the worst possible" for [Williams](/teams/williams).

The recovery of the day came from row nine. The rookie [Fernando Alonso](/drivers/fernando-alonso) started eighteenth, ran a one-stop that nobody around him copied, and finished ninth for [Aston Martin](/teams/aston-martin)'s only points of the weekend. An amazing result from the Spaniard who was fighting Cadillacs just a few weekends ago. [Nico Hulkenberg](/drivers/nico-hulkenberg) did what Nico Hulkenberg always does, an amazing and careful race which turned thirteenth on the grid into eighth for [Audi](/teams/audi). A well deserved result as some repayment for the power unit that ended his sprint on Saturday. [Liam Lawson](/drivers/liam-lawson) took seventh in the Red Bull, bringing home a ten-second penalty for ignoring a yellow flag, in a car he had never driven before Friday. An amazing result to prove to his seniors that he deserves his spot at least at the junior [Racing Bulls](/teams/racing-bulls) team.

[Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:14.230 on lap 60, and finished fifth. To no one's surprise was yet again a menace to be around. A risky overtake over Hamilton at lap 1, forcing the 7-time champion to take evasive action and force Verstappen onto the grass. Then on the final lap, a deployment of energy in the heavy recharge sector at turn 6 almost ended in a double-DNF for the Ferraris. [Oscar Piastri](/drivers/oscar-piastri) was sixth, fifteen seconds behind the Ferraris he started ahead of, and is now 55 points behind his own team-mate.

## What it did to the championship

Antonelli leaves the Netherlands on 242. Russell and Hamilton are both on 183, separated only by Russell's two wins to Hamilton's one, and Norris is fourth on 159. The lead is 59 points with eleven rounds to go, which is not safe, but it is the sort of margin that turns a season into an exercise in not making mistakes. The only driver convincing me he can challenge the almost 20-year old, is Norris. Russell is Toto's good boy and will do as he is told, Hamilton is most probably yet another bright star that dims under Ferrari's strategies and ignorance.

The two men who did most to make the race interesting are the two furthest from winning the title. Norris has won the last two Grands Prix and is still 83 adrift. Verstappen scored nothing and sits sixth on 112, which after Zandvoort is not a championship position, it is a season.

[Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) lead the constructors' table on 425 from [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) on 338 and McLaren on 263. Two Mercedes on the podium and a Ferrari fourth and fifth is the shape this season keeps taking, and Sunday showed why it is so hard to break: McLaren had the fastest car at the end of the race and still only matched Mercedes' haul, 33 points each, because they only had one car near the front. Matching the leaders when you are 162 behind them is not progress.

## Where it leaves us

**For the books:** the last Formula 1 race at Circuit Zandvoort, Norris' second win in a row and his second at this track after 2024, Verstappen out on lap one of his home Grand Prix, a red flag before anyone had completed a lap, two power unit failures in one weekend (Hulkenberg's in the sprint, Bearman's before the restart), six retirements, only seven cars on the lead lap, and a team order that decided three points between championship rivals in the same garage.

The full classification is on the [race page](/series/f1/weekend/12/race), Saturday's is on the [sprint page](/series/f1/weekend/12/sprint), the rest of the weekend is on the [Dutch Grand Prix hub](/series/f1/weekend/12), and the running totals are on the [standings](/series/f1/standings). [Motorsport.com has the full set of results and standings](https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/all-the-results-and-standings-from-the-2026-f1-dutch-grand-prix/10848632/), and The Race has its [winners and losers](https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/winners-and-losers-from-f1-2026-dutch-gp/).

Zandvoort came back in 2021 and spent most of the time since being told it was too narrow for modern Formula 1. It ends with a sprint won from a four-hundredths pole, a Grand Prix decided by an overtake at Turn 1 and a call from a pit wall, and its own driver in the barrier at the last corner on the first lap. Too narrow for overtaking, and it still produced more incident in one weekend than circuits twice its width manage in a season. It deserved better than a goodbye.

title: F1 Italian GP 2026: FP1 - Ferrari one-two in the Monza morning, and four cars handed to somebody else
summary: Charles Leclerc led Lewis Hamilton in first practice at Monza, giving Ferrari the top two places at their home race before anything counted. Four teams sat a race driver out to give a rookie the hour, which is the rule doing exactly what it was written to do.
body:
First practice at [Monza](/series/f1/weekend/13) is the least reliable hour of the weekend and the most watched one at this circuit, because for one morning a year the timing screen can be made to say the right thing. On Friday it did. [Charles Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) put a **1:23.008** on the board, [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton) followed him 0.173s later, and [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) headed a session at their own Grand Prix.

It meant nothing by Sunday afternoon. It was worth having anyway.

## The order

| Pos | Driver | Team | Gap | Laps |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | [Charles Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) | [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) | 1:23.008 | 29 |
| 2 | [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton) | [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) | +0.173 | 26 |
| 3 | [George Russell](/drivers/george-russell) | [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) | +0.304 | 27 |
| 4 | [Liam Lawson](/drivers/liam-lawson) | [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) | +0.425 | 26 |

| 10 | Paul Aron | [Alpine](/teams/alpine) | +1.169 | 23 |

| 13 | [Nico Hulkenberg](/drivers/nico-hulkenberg) | [Audi](/teams/audi) | +1.618 | 27 |
| 14 | [Oliver Bearman](/drivers/oliver-bearman) | [Haas](/teams/haas) | +1.638 | 28 |
| 15 | Luke Browning | [Williams](/teams/williams) | +1.732 | 25 |
| 16 | [Carlos Sainz](/drivers/carlos-sainz) | [Williams](/teams/williams) | +1.819 | 25 |
| 17 | Ayumu Iwasa | [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) | +1.865 | 24 |
| 18 | [Esteban Ocon](/drivers/esteban-ocon) | [Haas](/teams/haas) | +2.844 | 26 |
| 19 | [Valtteri Bottas](/drivers/valtteri-bottas) | [Cadillac](/teams/cadillac) | +2.976 | 27 |
| 20 | [Lance Stroll](/drivers/lance-stroll) | [Aston Martin](/teams/aston-martin) | +3.058 | 23 |
| 21 | [Fernando Alonso](/drivers/fernando-alonso) | [Aston Martin](/teams/aston-martin) | +3.064 | 21 |
| 22 | [Colton Herta](/drivers/colton-herta) | [Cadillac](/teams/cadillac) | +6.914 | 5 |

[Formula 1's own report](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/fp1-leclerc-leads-hamilton-and-russell-during-first-practice-at-the-italian-grand-prix.7DUTqVtZlb4zvqNfBsyl1t) had it the same way. [George Russell](/drivers/george-russell) was third for [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) at +0.304 and would go on to top both of the sessions that followed, which in hindsight is the only line on this sheet that predicted anything.

## Four teams gave a car away

Look at tenth, fifteenth, seventeenth and twenty-second. Paul Aron in the [Alpine](/teams/alpine), Luke Browning in the [Williams](/teams/williams), Ayumu Iwasa in the [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) and Colton Herta in the [Cadillac](/teams/cadillac). None of them has a race seat. All four were in a car on Friday morning because the regulations say they have to be.

Every full-time driver must stand aside for a rookie in two practice sessions a season, which works out at four outings per team across the year, and Monza is a popular place to spend one. We wrote the rule up in [how a Formula 1 race weekend works](/information/formula-1/how-a-formula-1-race-weekend-works) before the weekend started, largely because it is the sort of thing that makes a Friday timing sheet unreadable if you do not know it is coming.

So [Pierre Gasly](/drivers/pierre-gasly), [Max Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen), [Alexander Albon](/drivers/alexander-albon) and [Sergio Perez](/drivers/sergio-perez) all watched the first hour from the garage. Gasly took pole position the next day without having turned a wheel on Friday morning, which is either a compliment to Alpine's simulator or a comment on how little this session is worth.

![Sergio Perez's Cadillac on track at Monza during 2026 Italian Grand Prix qualifying](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Sergio_Perez_2026_Italian_Grand_Prix_qualifying.jpg/1280px-Sergio_Perez_2026_Italian_Grand_Prix_qualifying.jpg)

*Perez in the Cadillac during qualifying on Saturday, the day after Colton Herta had the car for this session. Eustace Bagge, [CC BY 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sergio_Perez_2026_Italian_Grand_Prix_qualifying.jpg), via Wikimedia Commons.*

Herta's hour was the shortest of anyone's: **five laps** and +6.914, which is a garage problem rather than a driver one. Aron's tenth on twenty-three laps was the best of the four, and comfortably ahead of the race driver in the other Alpine on outright pace over a single lap.

## Lawson, fourth, in a car he is still learning

[Liam Lawson](/drivers/liam-lawson) was fourth. He is in the Red Bull because [Isack Hadjar](/drivers/isack-hadjar) is not, and at Zandvoort a fortnight ago he had never driven the 2026 car at all and finished the only practice session fourteenth. One weekend later he was 0.425s off the top of the sheet with the second Red Bull entry given over to Iwasa for the morning.

He started Sunday's race from the pit lane and finished fourteenth, so the Friday was the best part of his weekend. It usually is when you are the newest thing in the garage.

![Liam Lawson on track at Monza in a Racing Bulls car](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b0/Liam_Lawson_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg/1280px-Liam_Lawson_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg)

*Lawson at Monza in 2025, in the Racing Bulls. He spent this weekend in the other car. Eustace Bagge, [CC BY 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Liam_Lawson_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg), via Wikimedia Commons.*

## What it was actually worth

Nothing, on the evidence. Ferrari's one-two became fourth and fifth in qualifying, **third and fourth on the grid**, and a retirement on the second lap of the Grand Prix. Antonelli was fifth here, seventh in qualifying, nineteenth on the grid, and won the race. Gasly did not set a lap and took pole position by the end of Saturday.

That is Monza in a sentence. The lap is so short and the tow so valuable that a Friday morning time tells you who turned up, roughly, and almost nothing else.

**For the books:** a Ferrari one-two in first practice at their home race, four rookies in four cars under the mandatory-outing rule, Colton Herta's five laps the shortest session of anybody's, and the man who would take pole the next day not turning a wheel all morning.

The full session is on the [Practice 1 page](/series/f1/weekend/13/practice-1), the rest of the weekend is on the [Italian Grand Prix hub](/series/f1/weekend/13), and the running totals are on the [standings](/series/f1/standings).

title: F1 Italian GP 2026: FP2 - Mercedes turn up in the afternoon, and the man who takes pole is fourteenth
summary: George Russell led second practice at Monza from Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli, with the field covered by less than three seconds. Pierre Gasly was fourteenth and Max Verstappen ninth, which tells you precisely how much a Friday afternoon at this circuit is worth.
body:
The tow makes Monza lie. Get a run in behind somebody on a quiet lap and you find three tenths that are not really yours; take your lap in clean air and you look slower than you are. Second practice on Friday afternoon is where that distortion is at its worst, because everybody is chasing a low-fuel number at once.

With that health warning attached: [George Russell](/drivers/george-russell) went quickest, and by Saturday lunchtime he had done it again.

## The order

| Pos | Driver | Team | Gap | Laps |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | [George Russell](/drivers/george-russell) | [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) | 1:22.559 | 31 |

The whole field inside **2.694s**, and the top six inside half a second. Monza compresses everything, which is why the circuit keeps producing qualifying sessions decided by hundredths and races decided by something else entirely.

All twenty-two regular drivers were back in the cars, [Formula 1 noted](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/fp2-russell-beats-leclerc-and-antonelli-to-the-fastest-time-in-free-practice-2-ahead-of-italian-grand-prix.4mVLF757oe0NuWE9Caw1wO), after four of them sat out the morning for rookies. [Russell](/drivers/george-russell) aborted his first run on softs to come in for a front wing adjustment and the lap he set afterwards was never beaten. [Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) spun at the second chicane inside the last ten minutes and rejoined without damage. [Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) spent his afternoon complaining about understeer and was still third.

## The three names worth marking

[Pierre Gasly](/drivers/pierre-gasly) was **fourteenth**, 1.214s off Russell, in an [Alpine](/teams/alpine) that had shown nothing all day. Twenty-four hours later he was on pole position at this circuit by six hundredths of a second. Nothing in this session forecast that, and anybody claiming otherwise is reading backwards.

![Pierre Gasly's Alpine on track at Monza](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Pierre_Gasly_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_Qualifying.jpg/1280px-Pierre_Gasly_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_Qualifying.jpg)

*Gasly at Monza a year earlier, in 2025. Eustace Bagge, [CC BY 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pierre_Gasly_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_Qualifying.jpg), via Wikimedia Commons.*

[Max Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen) was ninth, which for [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) at a low-drag circuit is worse than it sounds. He finished the race third.

[Kimi Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) was third, 0.141s off his own team-mate, and had the second-largest lap count in the session at thirty-two. That mattered more than the time. He already knew he was taking a full new power unit and starting near the back on Sunday, so Friday afternoon was not about a single lap for him. It was about learning what the car would do in traffic on a circuit where he would be spending the whole afternoon in it.

## Ferrari were still there

[Charles Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) second and [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton) fifth, so [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) had both cars in the top five for the second session running. That is a genuinely good Friday by the standards of their season, and it came with an engine step brought specifically for this weekend under the in-season upgrade allowance the 2026 rules provide.

They qualified fourth and fifth. Leclerc did not complete the second lap of the race.

## The bit that never shows up on the sheet

Ten teams declared **26 new parts** to the FIA for this weekend, and eleven of those, from six teams, were filed under drag range or drag reduction. Friday afternoon is when you find out whether taking the wings off actually worked, and the answer at Monza is always the same: the low-drag cars look quick in a straight line and vague everywhere else, and the lap time lands wherever the compromise lands.

You can read the full declaration on the [technical file for the weekend](/series/f1/weekend/13). It is the most honest document of any Grand Prix, because teams have to say what they changed and why.

**For the books:** Russell's first of two, the field covered by 2.694s, Gasly fourteenth on the Friday before his maiden pole, Verstappen ninth, and both Ferraris in the top five for the second session in a row.

The full session is on the [Practice 2 page](/series/f1/weekend/13/practice-2), Friday morning is on the [Practice 1 page](/series/f1/weekend/13/practice-1), and the rest of the weekend is on the [Italian Grand Prix hub](/series/f1/weekend/13).

*Cover photo: Russell in practice at Monza in 2025. Eustace Bagge, [CC BY 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:George_Russell_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg), via Wikimedia Commons.*

title: F1 Italian GP 2026: FP3 - Russell makes it two from two, and the top eight are covered by half a second
summary: George Russell led final practice at Monza as well, from Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen, with eight cars inside 0.554s of each other. It set up a qualifying hour that nobody could call, and produced a pole position nobody did.
body:
Saturday morning at Monza is the last hour before it counts. Parc fermé closes at the end of it, the fuel loads come down, and the timing screen finally starts telling something close to the truth. What it said was that [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) were the quickest thing at the circuit and that seven other cars were near enough to make qualifying a lottery.

Both halves of that turned out to be true. Neither produced the result anyone expected.

## The order

| Pos | Driver | Team | Gap | Laps |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| 1 | [George Russell](/drivers/george-russell) | [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) | 1:22.219 | 13 |
| 2 | [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton) | [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) | +0.226 | 21 |
| 3 | [Max Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen) | [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) | +0.350 | 24 |
| 4 | [Kimi Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) | [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) | +0.361 | 18 |
| 5 | [Lando Norris](/drivers/lando-norris) | [McLaren](/teams/mclaren) | +0.406 | 18 |

| 12 | [Liam Lawson](/drivers/liam-lawson) | [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) | +0.984 | 23 |
| 13 | [Gabriel Bortoleto](/drivers/gabriel-bortoleto) | [Audi](/teams/audi) | +1.079 | 21 |
| 14 | [Oliver Bearman](/drivers/oliver-bearman) | [Haas](/teams/haas) | +1.366 | 23 |
| 15 | Yuki Tsunoda | [Racing Bulls](/teams/racing-bulls) | +1.598 | 16 |
| 16 | [Carlos Sainz](/drivers/carlos-sainz) | [Williams](/teams/williams) | +1.656 | 28 |

| 22 | [Lance Stroll](/drivers/lance-stroll) | [Aston Martin](/teams/aston-martin) | +3.336 | 20 |

**0.554s** covering the top eight, and five different teams inside it. [Russell](/drivers/george-russell) set his time on **thirteen laps**, fewer than anybody else in the top twelve, which is the sort of detail that reads as confidence.

## Two drivers who already knew where they were starting

[Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) was fourth and [Alexander Albon](/drivers/alexander-albon) eighteenth, and both of them were going to line up at the back on Sunday for taking new engines. Albon lost part of the session to a steering wheel problem that had the [Williams](/teams/williams) wheeled back into the garage, then spent the end of it towing [Carlos Sainz](/drivers/carlos-sainz) down the straight, and [both were investigated afterwards](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/fp3-russell-goes-fastest-from-hamilton-and-verstappen-in-final-italy-practice.6i9o4gazCqUo3UtLVRgoe8) over a yellow flag.

![Alexander Albon's Williams on track at Monza](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Alexander_Albon_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg/1280px-Alexander_Albon_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg)

*Albon in final practice at Monza in 2025. Eustace Bagge, [CC BY 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Alexander_Albon_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg), via Wikimedia Commons.*

There was needle elsewhere too. [Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen) complained about a Ferrari being permanently in his way, Russell was looked at for impeding [Piastri](/drivers/oscar-piastri) and cleared, and Hamilton and Verstappen went side by side down the main straight and arrived at Turn 2 in a mood. On a lap this short with twenty-two cars looking for a tow, Saturday morning at Monza is mostly a traffic-management exercise.

## Gasly, ninth, and about to embarrass everybody

Ninth in final practice. Fourteenth on Friday afternoon. Then a **1:21.786** in Q3 and the first pole position of his career.

There is no reading of this session that saw it coming, and it is worth being honest about that rather than reverse-engineering a signal. What [Alpine](/teams/alpine) had was a car set up for one thing, at the one circuit where that thing is the whole lap, and a driver who put it together when the fuel came out. Practice does not reward that. Qualifying does.

## Ferrari's last good session

[Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton) second and [Charles Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) sixth meant [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) had been in the top six of all three practice sessions at their home Grand Prix. Hamilton has won at this circuit five times, a record he shares with Michael Schumacher, and this was the weekend Ferrari marked thirty years since Schumacher joined them and twenty since his last Monza win for them.

They qualified fourth and fifth. Leclerc was in the barriers at the Parabolica on lap two and Hamilton finished sixth. The tifosi got Saturday morning and not much else.

## What it actually set up

Three sessions, two different leaders, and a Q3 order that matched none of them. [Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) was fourth here and set the fastest lap of anybody in Q2, and started the race nineteenth because of a power unit penalty his team took deliberately at his home race. [Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen) was third here and third on Sunday, the only driver all weekend whose Saturday morning form survived contact with the result.

If you want the mechanics of why a Saturday morning at Monza predicts so little, the format itself is laid out in [how a Formula 1 race weekend works](/information/formula-1/how-a-formula-1-race-weekend-works).

**For the books:** Russell's second session win of the weekend on thirteen laps, the top eight inside 0.554s across five teams, Ferrari in the top six of every practice session at their home race, and the eventual polesitter ninth.

The full session is on the [Practice 3 page](/series/f1/weekend/13/practice-3), qualifying is on the [Qualifying page](/series/f1/weekend/13/qualifying), and the rest of the weekend is on the [Italian Grand Prix hub](/series/f1/weekend/13).

*Cover photo: Verstappen in final practice at Monza in 2025. Eustace Bagge, [CC BY 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Max_Verstappen_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg), via Wikimedia Commons.*

title: F1 Italian GP 2026: Qualifying - Nine years for six hundredths: Gasly puts an Alpine on pole at Monza
summary: Pierre Gasly took the first pole position of his career at the circuit where he took his first win, beating George Russell by 0.060s. Kimi Antonelli was quickest of anybody in Q2, went slower in Q3 than he had in Q2, and lined up nineteenth anyway.
body:
[Pierre Gasly](/drivers/pierre-gasly) had been to Monza before and left with something. In 2020 he won here, from tenth, in a Toro Rosso, in the strangest race of that season. On Saturday he came back and took the first pole position of his career at the same circuit, and did it with a lap nobody in the paddock had any reason to expect.

**1:21.786.** Six hundredths of a second clear of a Mercedes that had led both of the sessions that mattered. He had been fourteenth on Friday afternoon and ninth that morning.

"It's been nine years trying to chase and get the opportunity to take pole position," he [told Formula 1 afterwards](https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/gasly-charges-to-sensational-maiden-f1-pole-at-monza-over-russell-and-piastri.4CKkkbvgmqL04ijMNBfuXF). He was third after the opening Q3 runs and produced the lap on the final one.

## The order

| Pos | Driver | Team | Q1 | Q2 | Q3 |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Pierre Gasly](/drivers/pierre-gasly) | [Alpine](/teams/alpine) | 1:22.612 | 1:22.077 | 1:21.786 |
| 2 | [George Russell](/drivers/george-russell) | [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) | 1:22.779 | 1:22.161 | 1:21.846 |
| 3 | [Oscar Piastri](/drivers/oscar-piastri) | [McLaren](/teams/mclaren) | 1:22.924 | 1:22.017 | 1:21.966 |
| 4 | [Charles Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) | [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) | 1:22.902 | 1:22.509 | 1:22.004 |
| 5 | [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton) | [Ferrari](/teams/ferrari) | 1:22.847 | 1:22.516 | 1:22.011 |
| 6 | [Max Verstappen](/drivers/max-verstappen) | [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) | 1:22.631 | 1:22.188 | 1:22.070 |
| 7 | [Kimi Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) | [Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) | 1:22.758 | **1:21.882** | 1:22.093 |
| 8 | [Franco Colapinto](/drivers/franco-colapinto) | [Alpine](/teams/alpine) | 1:22.662 | 1:22.400 | 1:22.220 |
| 9 | [Lando Norris](/drivers/lando-norris) | [McLaren](/teams/mclaren) | 1:22.659 | 1:22.067 | 1:22.256 |
| 10 | [Arvid Lindblad](/drivers/arvid-lindblad) | [Racing Bulls](/teams/racing-bulls) | 1:22.727 | 1:22.345 | 1:22.286 |
| 11 | [Gabriel Bortoleto](/drivers/gabriel-bortoleto) | [Audi](/teams/audi) | 1:22.946 | 1:22.517 | |
| 12 | [Oliver Bearman](/drivers/oliver-bearman) | [Haas](/teams/haas) | 1:22.906 | 1:22.756 | |
| 13 | [Nico Hulkenberg](/drivers/nico-hulkenberg) | [Audi](/teams/audi) | 1:23.440 | 1:22.779 | |
| 14 | [Liam Lawson](/drivers/liam-lawson) | [Red Bull](/teams/red-bull-racing) | 1:22.989 | 1:22.821 | |
| 15 | [Carlos Sainz](/drivers/carlos-sainz) | [Williams](/teams/williams) | 1:23.616 | 1:23.453 | |
| 16 | [Esteban Ocon](/drivers/esteban-ocon) | [Haas](/teams/haas) | 1:23.466 | 1:23.454 | |
| 17 | Yuki Tsunoda | [Racing Bulls](/teams/racing-bulls) | 1:23.755 | | |
| 18 | [Alexander Albon](/drivers/alexander-albon) | [Williams](/teams/williams) | 1:24.356 | | |
| 19 | [Valtteri Bottas](/drivers/valtteri-bottas) | [Cadillac](/teams/cadillac) | 1:24.364 | | |
| 20 | [Sergio Perez](/drivers/sergio-perez) | [Cadillac](/teams/cadillac) | 1:24.595 | | |
| 21 | [Fernando Alonso](/drivers/fernando-alonso) | [Aston Martin](/teams/aston-martin) | 1:25.150 | | |
| 22 | [Lance Stroll](/drivers/lance-stroll) | [Aston Martin](/teams/aston-martin) | 1:25.222 | | |

Ten cars inside half a second in Q3. Both [Alpines](/teams/alpine) in the top eight, which has not been a sentence worth writing this season. And the bold number in the middle of the table is the one to keep hold of, because it belongs to the driver who qualified seventh and started nineteenth.

## The man who stopped trying, and started nineteenth

Look at Q2 rather than Q3. [Kimi Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) went **1:21.882** in the middle segment, quicker than anybody else managed in Q2 and quicker than eight of the ten Q3 laps that followed. Then in Q3 he went **1:22.093**, two tenths slower than his own Q2 time, qualified seventh, and started the race **nineteenth**.

A driver does not go slower in the segment that decides the grid by accident. He already knew where he was starting.

![Kimi Antonelli's Mercedes on track at Monza](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/Andrea_Kimi_Antonelli_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg/1280px-Andrea_Kimi_Antonelli_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg)

*Antonelli at Monza in 2025. Eustace Bagge, [CC BY 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Andrea_Kimi_Antonelli_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_FP3.jpg), via Wikimedia Commons.*

[Mercedes](/teams/mercedes) had decided at Zandvoort to take a full new power unit for him here, which carries a grid penalty, and to do it at the race he would most want to start from the front. Toto Wolff had explained the arithmetic without dressing it up: the calculations said Monza was the best track to spend it, and algorithms do not take a driver's nationality into account.

Antonelli's own read was that starting at the back "in some ways helps to release pressure", though he would very much rather have been fighting for pole. He thought a top five was realistic.

## What the grid actually looked like

Qualifying and the grid are two different documents, and at Monza they disagreed badly. The FIA's [final starting grid](/series/f1/weekend/13/qualifying) carried five penalties:

| Car | Penalty | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Antonelli | **30 places** | additional power unit elements |
| Albon | 20 places | additional power unit elements |
| Lawson | 35 places, then **pit lane** | additional power unit elements, then car modified under parc ferme |
| Alonso | **pit lane** | car modified under parc ferme, additional power unit elements |
| Piastri | 3 places | impeding |

Which turned the order into this:

| | Qualified | Started |
|---|---:|---|
| Gasly | 1 | 1 |
| Russell | 2 | 2 |
| Piastri | 3 | 6 |
| Leclerc | 4 | 3 |
| Hamilton | 5 | 4 |
| Verstappen | 6 | 5 |
| Antonelli | 7 | **19** |
| Norris | 9 | 8 |
| Lawson | 14 | **pit lane** |
| Alonso | 21 | **pit lane** |

The front row stood, the next four shuffled, and only twenty cars lined up on the grid at all because two of them started from the pit lane.

## Piastri lost three places for getting in Lawson's way

The one penalty here that was not about engines is worth reading, because the stewards did something slightly unusual with it. [Oscar Piastri](/drivers/oscar-piastri) impeded [Liam Lawson](/drivers/liam-lawson) at Turn 2 during qualifying, a breach of Article B4.1.1, and took the standard three-place drop.

What makes it interesting is the reasoning. On leaving the pits Piastri was told over the radio to watch for Verstappen and Lawson as he joined, but not that they were on push laps. He worked out Verstappen was coming, slowed, kept right and let him through, and could do nothing about Lawson behind. The stewards accepted that he "had, at this stage, no other options available" and that the impeding was inadvertent, and gave him the three places anyway, because the penalty for impeding is a standard one and intention does not enter into it.

![Oscar Piastri's McLaren on track at Monza](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Oscar_Piastri_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_qualifying.jpg/1280px-Oscar_Piastri_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_qualifying.jpg)

*Piastri qualifying at Monza in 2025. Eustace Bagge, [CC BY 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Oscar_Piastri_2025_Italian_Grand_Prix_qualifying.jpg), via Wikimedia Commons.*

So the driver who qualified third started sixth for a mistake the stewards agreed he could not avoid. That is the rule working exactly as written, and it is still hard to look at.

## Ferrari, fourth and fifth, at home

[Charles Leclerc](/drivers/charles-leclerc) and [Lewis Hamilton](/drivers/lewis-hamilton) were separated by **0.007s** and lined up third and fourth once the penalties shook out. For a team that had been in the top six of all three practice sessions with a new engine step, second row at their own Grand Prix was a reasonable return and an underwhelming one at the same time.

Hamilton has more pole positions at Monza than anyone. He did not add to them, and neither Ferrari saw the end of the race in the position it started.

## Our view

Gasly's lap is the best single piece of driving of the weekend and it will be remembered for about a fortnight, because of what happened on Sunday. That is the shape of a Monza pole: it is worth an enormous amount on Saturday evening and rather less at four o'clock the following afternoon, at a circuit where the slipstream gives the car behind a weapon the car in front cannot answer.

He led the opening laps. He finished seventh.

**For the books:** Gasly's first pole in nine years of trying and at the circuit of his first win, both Alpines in the top eight, ten cars inside half a second in Q3, Leclerc and Hamilton split by seven thousandths, and the fastest Q2 lap of anybody belonging to a driver who started nineteenth.

The full session is on the [Qualifying page](/series/f1/weekend/13/qualifying), Saturday morning is on the [Practice 3 page](/series/f1/weekend/13/practice-3), the race is on the [race page](/series/f1/weekend/13/race), and the running totals are on the [standings](/series/f1/standings).

*Cover photo: Gasly during this qualifying session, Monza, 5 September 2026. Eustace Bagge, [CC BY 4.0](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pierre_Gasly_2026_Italian_Grand_Prix_qualifying_-_1.jpg), via Wikimedia Commons.*

title: Sixty years, and a nineteenth place: Antonelli wins at Monza for Italy
summary: Kimi Antonelli started the Italian Grand Prix nineteenth and won it, the first Italian to win at Monza since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966. Charles Leclerc put his Ferrari into the Parabolica barriers on lap two and Pierre Gasly led away from his first pole before finishing seventh.
body:
The last Italian to win a Formula 1 race at Monza was Ludovico Scarfiotti, in a Ferrari, in 1966. Nobody has managed it since, through the whole of the sport's modern history, and a fair amount of national effort has gone into trying. On Sunday a twenty-year-old from Bologna did it in a Mercedes, having started nineteenth.

[Kimi Antonelli](/drivers/kimi-antonelli) won the [Italian Grand Prix](/series/f1/weekend/13) by 3.857s from his own team-mate, in the seventh victory of his season, on the one weekend of the year his team had decided in advance he would be starting near the back.

## The result

| Pos | Driver | Team | Gap | Pts |
|---:|---|---|---|---:|
